issues.where: data/public/dossiers/rural-hypertension-group/prior_project.md, Participant accounting: "four who died before assessment"; subsequent analysis: "A sensitivity analysis using multiple imputation for missing endpoints gave an adjusted difference of −5.5 mmHg". dossier.yaml F08/F11.
issues.problem: The report puts deaths among the 72 absent endpoints and then describes imputation for missing endpoints under an ordinary observed-variable missingness assumption, without saying how deaths were treated or what population the BP contrast targets. Six-month BP after death does not exist; it cannot simply be treated as an unobserved living-person measurement. The supplied sensitivity estimate is therefore scientifically ambiguous, especially because the stretch brief explicitly asks the writer to build on this missing-data expertise.
issues.fix: Make the fictional historical analysis explicit: 'The four deaths were handled as terminal events and were not assigned or imputed six-month BP values. The multiple-imputation analysis was restricted to the 476 participants alive at six months, imputing the 68 missing measurements among those survivors. It estimated a survivor-conditional adjusted contrast of −5.5 mmHg (95% CI −9.6 to −1.4), under an observed-variable missingness assumption among survivors. Both this contrast and the observed-endpoint analysis may be affected by post-randomization survival/attendance selection and do not estimate a treatment effect for all 480 enrollees.' Distinguish terminal events from missing measurements in F08 and carry the restricted population and limitations into F10/F11 and the primary-publication summary. Do not describe this as an all-participant intention-to-treat robustness check.
